title: Grateful Dead Live at Ice Palace on 1969-03-29

ai_review.summary: Fair‑sounding soundboard capture of the March 29 1969 Ice Palace show, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and a powerful Eleven.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that suffers from tape‑age muddiness, hiss and several splices, but it remains listenable enough to showcase the band’s early psychedelic fire. Fans repeatedly praise the second half – especially the Dark Star outro, The Eleven and Doin’ That Rag – and note Jerry’s soaring leads and Phil’s booming bass. Overall the performance is praised despite the technical flaws of the tape.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is generally praised (≈4‑5 ★) while recording quality is noted as muddy and spliced (≈2‑3 ★). Weighted average yields a solid mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muddy, tape‑like sound with noticeable hiss; several splices cut out portions of Dark Star; low tom‑cymbal mix; missing bits but overall decent balance for a 1969 reel‑to‑reel capture.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early psychedelic set that builds into the classic “Holy Trinity” (Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven) with an exploratory, high‑energy second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry Garcia’s soaring solos and beautiful guitar work, especially in Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh receives praise for “booming bass bombs” and sounding great throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Reference to Pigpen’s bluesy attitude adds flavor to the early show.
